Great Chinese Authentic Cuisine
Dec 2021
Value for money, The food is FRESH. The varieties are authentically curated. When in Ho Chi Minh City and when it is Chinese Authentic Cuisine, you are yearning for, Don't miss out the Shang Garden. The Culinary MUST.
We tried the Peking Duck, Roast Suckling Pig and varieties of Dim Sum. The Chef is from Hong Kong, Chef Lau. He recommended several Signature dishes. It is no surprise. The food is FRESH and excellent. Just Delicious.
Great job, Shang Garden.

So good we went twice!
Feb 2020 • Friends
Whilst walking around looking for somewhere to eat on our first night we came across their restaurant. What a find, lovely staff and amazing food. A little on the pricey side, mainly the wine, approx £25/30 for a brittle but this was quality Chilean Sauvignon . Had a amzing prawns , spinach rice with scallops and green beans to die for. It was so good we went again on our last night. 100% recommend!

It's not my favorite anymore
Apr 2017 • Family
Shang Garden used to be my favorite Chinese Restaurant in District 7. We visited there around 5 times in the past. But the last visit might be the last one there because everything has changed in a worse way. Food, especially dimsum was so bad with clammy skin and unfresh prawn; too much food flavouring and coloring for durian pudding. Un-professional staff and service. I feel so bad for this beautiful Restaurant.

First time food taste
Jan 2017 • Family
This restaurant opened more than 6 months I think. But is my first time visit. The decor is great but the food just soso. Got 3 stars from me is because of the decor. I tried dim sum, congee and noodles. Heard that the chef from Yeebo so not expect much from it. Congee and noodles were disaster. But the dumplings are acceptable. Lucky their pricing are still reasonable. So if you are nearby and need to find a quiet place for lunch, not a bad choice here. Will try other A la Carte next time and write another report.

Nice replacement for Ming Dynasty
Nov 2016 • Family
This new restaurant replace the well known Ming Dynasty and does not disappoint. They still serve great Beijing duck along with great chinese ala carte dishes. They add some Singaporean dishes. They serve Dim sum but just for lunch (don't really know why or who do they aim to serve at such late time)! The service is a lot better than when it was still Ming D. The food is a bit better in my opinion and the price is a lot more affordable. I have been back to this restaurant more time in the last month than I did for a year when it was still Ming.
